title: Webhook
body:
An inversion of the usual [[API]] direction: instead of you repeatedly polling their server asking "is it done yet?", their server calls **you** when the event happens. You register a URL with them; when something occurs (a payment settles, a review is moderated), they send an HTTP POST to that URL with a payload describing the event.

The detail that matters in interviews: webhooks are **server-to-server**. The receiving URL must be a publicly reachable server you control — not your browser, which has no address anyone can call. That also means webhook handlers need their own [[Authentication]] (usually a shared secret or signature header), because the endpoint is open to the internet and anyone could POST fake events to it. They should be idempotent too, since providers retry on failure; see [[Idempotent]].
